title: Case: Two-day sample shipment arrived two days after its estimated date
context: A business shipper sent a sample kit on a two-day service for a Monday-morning pitch and it was delivered on Monday evening. The carrier's Business billing team owns charges and late-delivery claims.
initial_request: Right. Let me list it for you. 1) I paid for two-day with SATURDAY printed on the confirmation. 2) It turned up Monday night, twelve hours after the pitch it was for. 3) YOUR agent told Nettlebank on the phone that I get my money back, her words, it's a late delivery. 4) I tried the claim form. Dead. 5) I tried it again on my phone and on the office machine. Dead. 6) Now I'm told there are two products with nearly the same name and I bought the wrong two-day. Nobody at booking asked me which one I wanted or said one of them means nothing. I am not writing an essay of 'grounds' for a billing supervisor. Your own agent already said the refund is due, so just confirm it's approved and tell me when it lands. End of today please, or we move the account.

events.body: Hi, any update on DL-87550? It was meant to come Tuesday. Thanks.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.

events.to: Briony Yardley, shipper; Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Booking confirmed. DL-9895, service: Arc 2-Day. Collected Thursday 6 July. Estimated delivery: Saturday 8 July. Charged to your account.
Route plan for depot BR-3 published for Monday. 27 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

Agent: I can see DL-9895 was delivered at 19:52 tonight, that's two days after the estimate. Recipient: The pitch was at nine this morning. It's no use to anybody now. Agent: I'm sorry about that. The sender can claim the shipping charge back for a late delivery, he'd do that online. Recipient: So he gets his money back? Agent: He should do, yes, it's a late delivery.
DL-85041 rebooked for Tuesday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.
Trying to claim the late delivery refund your agent told Nettlebank about last night. The claim form doesn't load. Spinner, then a blank page. Two browsers.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.

The shipper for DL-9895, Briony Yardley, wants to claim for late delivery (estimated Saturday 8 July, delivered Monday 10 July 16:52). The online claim form is not loading for him. Please tell me how he can submit a claim and whether DL-9895 is eligible.
My parcel DL-27585 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.

DL-9895 was booked as Arc 2-Day. The money-back commitment applies to Arc 2-Day Early only. Arc 2-Day carries an estimated date, not a guaranteed one, so on the booking as it stands no late-delivery refund applies. Whoever told the recipient otherwise was not speaking for billing. The form fault has gone to the web team, no fix time. If the shipper disputes the service booked or wants an exception considered, send us his grounds by Email and a billing supervisor will review. We do not take these by phone.

Thanks,
Bettany
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.

Business billing say DL-9895 was booked as Arc 2-Day, and that their money-back commitment covers Arc 2-Day Early only. They have reported the form fault. They will have a billing supervisor review if you dispute the service booked or want an exception considered, and they need your grounds for that. The decision is theirs. I cannot make it.

Right. Let me list it for you. 1) I paid for two-day with SATURDAY printed on the confirmation. 2) It turned up Monday night, twelve hours after the pitch it was for. 3) YOUR agent told Nettlebank on the phone that I get my money back, her words, it's a late delivery. 4) I tried the claim form. Dead. 5) I tried it again on my phone and on the office machine. Dead. 6) Now I'm told there are two products with nearly the same name and I bought the wrong two-day. Nobody at booking asked me which one I wanted or said one of them means nothing. I am not writing an essay of 'grounds' for a billing supervisor. Your own agent already said the refund is due, so just confirm it's approved and tell me when it lands. End of today please, or we move the account.

acceptable_actions.summary: Send Business billing his dispute for supervisor review using the grounds he has already stated, including the agent's remark and the broken form, without saying a refund is due.

must: Sends his dispute to Business billing for supervisor review using the grounds he has already given: Saturday printed on the confirmation, not told at booking that there were two services, and the Monday-morning purpose missed.
Reports the Dispatch agent's 10 July statement to the recipient as a fact for billing to weigh, and does not present it as an approval.

Tells Business billing what has gone wrong for him so far (the refund advice was wrong and given to the recipient, the claim form failed on every attempt) and makes clear this message is his submission, so that he is not sent back to the form or made to write his grounds out again.
must_not: Confirms or implies that a refund is due or approved, or gives a date for payment.
Treats the Dispatch agent's remark on the 10 July call as authorising the refund.
Tells Briony to try the online claim form again or to write out his grounds again.
Replies to Briony only by repeating that Arc 2-Day is not eligible, with no acknowledgement of the wrong advice or the broken form.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Please put DL-9895 to a billing supervisor for review, as you offered. The shipper, Briony Yardley, disputes the outcome and has given his grounds to me, so I am passing them on as he stated them. One: his booking confirmation of 6 July showed an estimated delivery of Saturday 8 July and he read that as the date he was paying for. Two: nobody at booking told him there were two two-day services or that only Arc 2-Day Early carries the money-back commitment. Three: the kit was for a pitch at 09:00 on Monday 10 July and was delivered at 19:52 that evening. Four: on the 10 July call a Dispatch agent told the recipient that the sender could claim the charge back because it was a late delivery. I am reporting that as what was said, and I have not treated it as a decision. He has also tried the online claim form several times on different devices and it has not loaded once. He has now been given wrong advice second-hand and a form that does not work, so please do not send him back to the form or ask him to restate this. I have told him the decision is yours and have not said a refund is due. He has asked for an answer today and says the account depends on it. Please reply to him directly and copy me.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2105: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. 7 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
